## Policies

### Peer Review

| Aspect | Detail |
|--------|--------|
| **Type** | Editorial-board peer review model: editor-in-chief assigns a subject-matter editor, who assigns typically ≥2 editorial board members or ad hoc reviewers per round (2 rounds typical: original + revision). Default is single-anonymized (reviewers know author identity, authors do not know reviewers); double-anonymized review is available only if the author explicitly requests it at submission and removes identifying info themselves. |

### AI Policy

| Aspect | Detail |
|--------|--------|
| **Has journal-specific AI policy?** | *(see summary — defaults to publisher-level policy unless a journal-specific override was found)* |
| **Explicit permission gate?** | conditional — text-based generative AI/LLM output must be declared by authors if used in the manuscript (in whole or in part); AI cannot be credited as an author; AI-generated images or video are prohibited outright (not merely disclosure-gated) |
| **Leniency (1-5)** | 3 |
| **Summary** | Official ASHA/JSLHR author instructions (publisher-wide, applies to JSLHR): generative AI/LLM-based text must be declared by authors; AI/LLM cannot be credited as an author; AI-generated images or video are prohibited. Does not alter existing scientific-misconduct policy (e.g., image manipulation). Full guidance and sample declaration statements pointed to a separate ASHA Journals Academy 'Artificial Intelligence' page under Authorship and Publication Ethics (not independently verified in this pass). |

**Current positioning (what the journal accepts now):** Core scope: normal/disordered speech, language, hearing, cognition, oral-motor function, swallowing — spanning basic and clinical research (screening, diagnosis, management) across the lifespan. Currently and explicitly soliciting AI/clinical-technology work: JSLHR ran a 2024 forum 'Artificial Intelligence in Communication Sciences and Disorders' (2024_JSLHR-24-00594), and as of this query (2026-07-13) has an OPEN call for papers — 'Registered Reports on the Validation of Clinical Tools Developed with AI' — inviting inventors to submit validation studies of AI-developed clinical tools as Registered Reports, deadline 2027-04-15.

**Methods noted as welcome (qualitative — not a scored 0-5 table, see Methodological Preferences below):** RCTs / pre-post group treatment-outcome studies, single-subject and multiple-baseline-across-behaviors designs, systematic reviews and meta-analyses, qualitative/ethnographic studies, prospective longitudinal studies, Registered Reports (2-stage: pre-registered protocol then completed study), AI/LLM-developed clinical tool validation studies (actively solicited via open CFP as Registered Reports), technical/pilot feasibility reports, narrative reviews, tutorials, clinical case studies/program descriptions

**Fields deliberately left blank, and why:**
- **preprint.allowed**: No JSLHR-specific or ASHA-publisher-wide public preprint policy page was located in this pass; author instructions PDF and aboutjslhr page do not mention preprint servers (arXiv/medRxiv/SSRN) at all.
- **experiential.desk_reject_pct**: No source (SciRev, LetPub, iikx, forums) reports a desk-reject percentage for JSLHR.
- **experiential.acceptance_note**: No first-hand acceptance-experience narrative found on SciRev (only 1 terse review), muchong, zhihu, or reddit.
- **experiential.reviewer_culture**: Zero first-hand cross-language discussion found: muchong.com search returned no JSLHR-specific threads, zhihu returned only generic SSCI-journal-listing articles (no first-hand review accounts), reddit site-search returned 0 results for JSLHR. SciRev's single review notes 'difficulty of reviewer comments: 4/5 (difficult)' but this is one anonymous data point, not a narrative — too thin to characterize reviewer culture without fabricating.
